analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md and docs/provider/cli-reference.md. No source, wire, key-handling or authorization code is in the supplied evidence. I read the head text of model-autopilot.md and the cli-reference patch plus its base text, and found no regression or contradiction with the threat model.

The model-autopilot.md additions (head lines 151, 175-212, 278-281, 293-297) describe selected-model recovery. The doc says recovery never evicts the ordinary selection, pins, held slots or advertised models that could load straight back, and that it waits while a live lease or pause manages residency. It also says an add-on hold (TB-012, T-059) pauses recovery and cancels an attempt in progress. An adoption can be released ten minutes after the hold expiry, and the released model is withdrawn and refuses new requests. The doc cites a policy 'pending owner review' in ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift.

This is a behavior-contract claim I could not verify. The doc says recovery 'may unload an adopted slot' that has no unexpired hold or in-flight request. Whether in-flight requests are drained and native retirement is preserved depends on source not supplied. The remaining integration questions are whether recovery's busy reason 'preload' interacts correctly with A-018 availability, and whether the add-on hold cancel path is race-free (T-059).

The cli-reference.md patch (head 961-963) documents a 15-second per-model shutdown unload wait. A model whose native retirement never finishes is left to process exit. This is availability and lifecycle behavior that relates to T-010 and T-028 (residual GPU data). It could leave memory unretired until exit, but the process exits anyway, so I identified no regression.

The cli-reference.md patch (head 1041-1056) adds the status output 'Configuration change needs a restart to apply' and 'Retrying <model>'. It exposes only local model IDs and timings to the local operator, with no new boundary exposure. The base_text unit for cli-reference.md has no changes beyond the patch.

No threat-model update is required beyond noting the new recovery path as a residency-changing actor. A reviewer of the underlying code should verify the claims about victim rules, in-flight protection and hold interaction.
